discussion.p: `std::simd::abs` accepts a basic_vec<T, Abi> where `T` models `signed_integral`. However, the result is defined in terms of `std::abs`, which accepts only standard signed integer types and types that promote to `int`. Restricting `std::simd::abs` to the types supported by `std::abs` would be a breaking design change, so perhaps `std::abs` could be bypassed. Also, `std::abs` may not return the same type as its arguments, so maybe the wording should contain an explicit cast.

blockquote.pre: template<signed_integral T, class Abi> constexpr basic_vec<T, Abi> abs(const basic_vec<T, Abi>& j);

blockquote.p: -8- Returns: An object where the ith element is initialized to the result of std::abs(j[i]) static_cast<T>(j[i] < 0 ? -j[i] : j[i]) for all i in the range `[0, size())`.
